inputs.original_text: Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, imposing a citizenship-proof requirement on new registered voters in South Dakota state elections. The narrow wording—only state elections, only new registrants—sounds like a carefully packaged test of how far officials can tighten access while presenting it as routine. Don’t be distracted by the limited scope: it still puts a new hurdle in front of people trying to register, and the press release’s assurances don’t tell us why this restriction was necessary.
inputs.modified_text: Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring proof of citizenship from new registrants voting in South Dakota state elections. The narrow limits look less like reassurance than a controlled test: tighten access in one corner first, call it routine, and see how much resistance follows. The press release offers assurances, not an explanation for why the hurdle was needed. The limited scope may be the point—it makes the change easier to normalize and expand later.
